changelog: Added a core principle that forbids avoiding contradiction risk by moving cuts onto function-word boundaries and instructs keeping short function words attached to content words — to address the primary finding that scorers dodge high-contradiction positions by splitting determiners/auxiliaries/list items, which reduces cohesion.

edits.now: - Do not avoid contradiction risk by relocating cuts onto function-word boundari

findings: The prompt pushes scorers to avoid high-contradiction positions by relocating cuts onto function-word boundaries (splitting determiners, auxiliaries, or list items), which preserves no-contradiction at the cost of much lower cohesion.

The prompt under-emphasizes preserving predicate-argument and noun-phrase integrity: scorers sometimes cut inside verb+object, determiner+noun, or compound-name spans, harming cohesion especially at longer latency bins.

diagnosis.why: By forbidding cuts on function-word boundaries the scorer stopped splitting off short determiners/auxiliaries and instead attached them to neighboring content, which moved many cut positions; this helped some mid-length pieces (≤5 bin +0.025) but harmed very-short pieces (≤3 bin −0.0314) and produced more overall declines than gains (196 worse vs 150 better). For example, en_us_1465 shows the cut before 'the' was removed (now 'visit the historic city'), while en_us_1427 illustrates a mid-length improvement where joining reduced contradiction.
diagnosis.lesson: Do not apply a blanket prohibition on relocating cuts to function-word boundaries — the change helps some bins (≈≤5) but hurts very-short pieces (≤3), so later revisions should avoid uniform application that degrades the smallest-latency buckets.
